answer: A ballot joins a cedar grove by staking $50 in a shared pool; any challenger proving it fake explodes it and pockets $50 — Upala's price-of-forgery game. A farm planting 10,000 ballots dies by the explosion check: one challenger drains $500,000 and every ballot is rejected and slashed. Each ballot needs a fresh vouch from a real member weekly, so the farm owes 10,000 vouches a week. The canyon between honest cost and farm profit is the bounty: faking one ballot pays a stranger $50 to unmask it, so the fable of cheap Sybils ends — a cedar grove stands only while every root is real.
